name: HMB (beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate)
short: A review says no studies have tested HMB toxicity in humans. Pooled 3-8 week studies (young and old) found no adverse blood test effects; a review in adults with cancer found no serious related harms.
text: A pooled analysis of safety data from nine studies in which adults were given HMB for 3 to 8 weeks found no adverse effect on any blood chemistry or haematology marker of tissue health and reported no untoward effects; compared with placebo, total and LDL cholesterol and systolic blood pressure fell slightly. A sports-nutrition position stand concluded that the available safety and toxicity data suggest oral HMB is safe in humans for up to at least one year, with no negative effects on glucose tolerance or insulin sensitivity. In a systematic review of 15 studies in adults with cancer, most of which gave HMB combined with amino acids or within oral nutritional supplements, no serious adverse effects directly related to the supplement were reported. A review of leucine and HMB in older people noted that no adverse events have been reported for HMB but that no studies have tested HMB toxicity in humans. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
